guard_streams.write_limit: Operator forecasts and planned network deployments are forward-looking and cannot be written as current parcel coverage or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2026 planned-network-deployments report on 13 May 2026.
The report examines full-fibre and gigabit-capable coverage anticipated by the end of 2028.
The report is based on operators' stated deployment plans as of January 2026 over the next three years.
The plans include privately funded deployments and deployments supported through public funds or intervention.
The report does not separately count national or local authority aspirations that are not operator deployment plans.
If all plans are realised, full fibre could reach 28.1 million homes, or 92%, by January 2029.
If all plans are realised, gigabit-capable coverage could reach 29 million homes, or 95%, by January 2029.
Rural gigabit-capable coverage is projected to rise from 2.9 million homes (66%) to 3.7 million (86%) if all plans are realised.
Ofcom estimates that 73% of homes could access at least two gigabit networks and 36% at least three by the end of 2028.
Around 6,950 additional geographically distinct FWA masts are planned or set for upgrade between January 2026 and January 2029.

guard_streams.source: Connected Nations - Planned Network Deployment background
guard_streams.write_limit: The statutory purpose, aggregation rules and confidentiality limits of planned-deployment reporting do not verify current postcode or parcel availability.

facts.detail: The PND report is explicitly forward-looking and supplements Ofcom's infrastructure reports.
Ofcom reports operator proposals for network deployment within the next three years.
The reporting duty is linked to section 134A of the Communications Act 2003.
The statutory scope includes new very high-capacity networks other than mobile networks.
The scope includes fixed-line or equivalent FWA upgrades intended to provide at least 100 Mbit/s download.
Ofcom describes future build proposals as confidential and extremely commercially sensitive.
Published information is aggregated and anonymised at UK, nation and local-authority levels.
The Secretary of State must consider infrastructure reports for public funding, national broadband plans and USO availability verification.
More specific operator and property-coverage data is sent to the Secretary of State but is not published.
Operator plans can change and the PND figures are not comprehensive or definitive.
